text:
evan: heads-up, ran into a reproducible Rollup/Vite/webpack interop bug with the JS SDK that only shows up when building for edge workers + d.ts bundling enabled. dev server ok, prod worker crashes with "TypeError: Redwood is not a constructor" or "ReferenceError: require is not defined" depending on bundler.

evan: minimal repro notes I put in the repo (private): vite + rollup-based build for library, consumer app target=webworker, install local sdk package. The SDK publish pipeline emits: dist/index.cjs.js, dist/index.esm.mjs, dist/index.d.ts (and we also generate a single combined types.d.ts via dts-bundle).

li: interesting — did you try swapping plugin order in the SDK rollup build? commonjs plugin before node-resolve often causes named import rewriting.

evan: yep. when rollup uses `@rollup/plugin-commonjs` before `@rollup/plugin-node-resolve` the esm output ends up wrapped in a cjs-interop shim that some bundlers later mis-handle. the published `index.esm.mjs` looked ESM but had a tiny wrapper function that references `module.exports` in a comment and that seems to trick webpack's resolver into choosing the cjs path.

sophia: also saw this earlier — tldr: plugin order matters. recommended rollup order for ESM-first build: node-resolve, replace, commonjs (last), terser. If you run commonjs too early it transforms dependencies into cjs and rollup emits weird wrappers.

kevin: another vector: the types bundling. our dts-bundle created a `types/index.d.ts` that contains `export = RedwoodClient;` style exports. Consumers with `esModuleInterop: false` get different runtime expectations and sometimes import the wrong shape -> `Redwood is not a constructor`. If we publish types that reflect the ESM named/default export shape, consumer TS configs line up.

li: packing both `export default` in the ESM and `module.exports =` in CJS can create a mismatch where some bundlers pick the wrong shape depending on `mainFields`. We should ensure ESM file uses `export default` and we provide `exports.import` -> './dist/index.esm.mjs' and `exports.require` -> './dist/index.cjs.js' with no wrapped shims in esm file.

ci-bot: nightly/sdk-bundle-e2e: failed on matrix entry rollup+vite+worker. Error: ReferenceError: require is not defined. Build artifacts attached: dist/index.esm.mjs, dist/index.cjs.js, dist/index.types.d.ts.

kevin: quick repro I used to debug differences: run `npx rollup -c` for the sdk with two configs: one with `preserveModules: true` and one without. With preserveModules the ESM output emits many small .mjs files and consumer bundlers resolve file-level conditions differently and actually prefer the ESM paths. Without preserveModules the single-file shim sometimes confuses webpack. Might be a viable mitigation for our SDK publish (more files but clearer resolution).

sophia: also check our package.json `exports` shape. If we add an explicit `exports.{"./package.json": "./package.json", ".": {"browser": "./dist/index.esm.mjs","import":"./dist/index.esm.mjs","require":"./dist/index.cjs.js"}}` it nudges bundlers to prefer the import/browser condition. Some bundlers still look at `main` so ensure `main` points to cjs but `module`/`browser`/`exports.import` point to the ESM.

li: consumer-side workarounds we documented for app teams: in vite app `optimizeDeps.include=['redwood-inference-js']` and in build `ssr.noExternal=['redwood-inference-js']` for SSR flows. For webpack, set `resolve.mainFields=['browser','module','main']`. But these are band-aids; SDK should be fixed.

kevin: additional oddity: when we generate combined d.ts via dts-bundle, the top of the file has `declare namespace RedwoodClient {}` and `export = RedwoodClient;` which forces consumers to use `import Redwood = require('redwood-inference-js')` in TS legacy style or enable `esModuleInterop`. Better to generate `export default class RedwoodClient {}` and `export * from './types'` for named exports parity. Types mismatch causes silent runtime shape errors.

ci-bot: test suggestion: add a CI job that runs `pnpm pack` on the SDK, then `npm ci` in three tiny consumer templates (vite worker, webpack worker, rollup worker) and runs the built worker in miniflare. Fail on any `require is not defined` or `is not a constructor` runtime errors. Run this across node 18/20 matrix.

li: agreed. also add a lint step that scans `dist/index.esm.mjs` for commonjs remnants: regex `\bmodule\.|require\(|exports\.` — fail publish if found.

sophia: short-term mitigation we can release: 1) rebuild ESM with plugin order fixed and no cjs wrappers, 2) publish `dist/edge.mjs` that simply `export { default } from './index.esm.mjs'; export * from './index.esm.mjs'` and map `exports."./edge"` -> `./dist/edge.mjs` so teams can import `redwood-inference-js/edge` as a stable edge-target entry. 3) regenerate types to be ESM-friendly.

evan: thanks — I'll open a single tracking issue that captures rollup plugin-order, preserveModules experiment, d.ts regeneration, exports mapping, and CI matrix request. I'll paste the small repro steps and the failing stack traces. cc @kevin for types help.

kevin: happy to help. once there's a candidate patch I can run the three consumer templates locally and validate. if we add the dist lint check and CI matrix, catch rate should be much higher.

sophia: also add a short DevEx doc page (internal) describing why `esModuleInterop` and `allowSyntheticDefaultImports` hide these problems and how to properly author packages to avoid relying on consumer TS flags.
